rule.signature: judgeLock(lock, probe, observerAwakeSeconds) -> alive | unresponsive | gone
rule.gone: the holder's pid isn't running, or ps -o lstart= -p <pid> differs from pid_start. Only gone counts as dead
rule.unresponsive: pid and start time match, the heartbeat is older than 90 s, and the observer has been awake at least 90 s since the Mac last woke
rule.observer_awake: seconds since kern.waketime, else kern.boottime: a stale heartbeat after a sleep never makes a live holder dead
rule.used_by: RAVIS for project_lock rows and for the checkout file; Clarvis for the file

lock_file.create: atomically, open(path, 'wx', 0o600), written by the process that actually writes: RAVIS for Codex sessions, the window for Clarvis-engine runs
lock_file.acquire: create the file, then obtain RAVIS's lock (on refusal delete the file and refuse), then heartbeat both every 15 s
lock_file.release: in reverse order, only after the holder's processes are confirmed gone and any settle is done; never while a switch holds the lock; never by a holder that has lost it

lock_file_leftover.rule: leftover lists the holding Codex session's recorded command processes, written by RAVIS at each look and emptied once they are confirmed gone; start is ps -o lstart= in the C locale. A window that finds a gone RAVIS holder ends exactly these, each individually by pid and start time, never by group, then confirms

verdict_cases.name: the holder's pid is not running
the pid was reused by a later process
an old heartbeat while the observer has been awake
an old heartbeat just after the Mac woke
a heartbeat exactly 90 s old is not older than 90 s
awake exactly 90 s counts as at least 90 s
not running wins over a fresh heartbeat after a wake

adoption_rule.records: RAVIS records its own instance, pid and process start time, in ravis_instance at every start
adoption_rule.rewrite_only_when: the checkout lock file still names RAVIS's previous instance
adoption_rule.otherwise: whatever the verdict, the file is left untouched, RAVIS's lock is marked superseded, the Codex session stays uncertain, and settle-claim, turns and resume get 409 LOCK_SUPERSEDED
adoption_rule.then: when the window releases, or registers its lock with adopt_file_lock true, RAVIS replaces the superseded row; the Codex session can then be settled by a window holding the lock, and continued

adoption_cases.name: the file names RAVIS's previous instance
a live window holds the file
an unresponsive window holds the file
a gone window holds the file
no file, and nothing else holds the root
no file, and a window won the create race

on_finding_a_lock.outcome: attach: never taken over; any window of the workspace joins the session and can stop it
reconcile: kill the recorded leftovers and running_command's group, confirm, continue the same task with continueOn, committing the leftovers first
refuse: another Clarvis window is working on this project
take over with a confirmation naming the window and its age
take over with a confirmation naming the window and its age

fence: a holder that lost its lock never commits, never writes the checkpoint, and never releases or rewrites a lock
stillHolds() is checked before every mutating tool call and before any commit or checkpoint write

lost means a heartbeat answered 409 LEASE_REVOKED, or the lock file no longer names this window; RAVIS unreachable is never loss: the run continues on the file, retries RAVIS every 15 s and re-registers with adopt_file_lock true
